key_insight: A small, clinically meaningful set of readily available features helped large language models do zero-shot chronic kidney disease screening better than using the full feature set.
clinical_relevance: This suggests LLMs could support practical, training-free CKD screening in community and resource-limited settings using minimal patient information.
method: Selected a compact feature subset using machine learning analysis
Serialized tabular patient records into standardized text prompts
Compared zero-shot performance of LLaMA-3, Qwen-3, Mistral, and GPT-4o-mini on full vs selected features
evidence_signal: The study tested four LLMs across three heterogeneous CKD datasets from three countries and found the selected feature set consistently improved balanced accuracy and probability estimates.
watch_item: Results are promising for screening, but real-world deployment still needs careful validation across populations and workflows before use.
paper_title: From Many to Meaningful: Feature-Guided Zero-Shot Chronic Kidney Disease Screening Using Large Language Models
